ambiguous_escalations.description: 5 clusters of near-duplicate StoryEntry rows (16 of 37 rows, 43%) sharing near-identical situation text but distinct titles/contentHash — e.g. 5 variants of an 'ANZ core banking transformation' story generated on 2026-07-21, 07-22, 07-23, 07-23, 07-31. All owned by the same cron/test account (c6c8d0163d973a8048e7e33b8). These are NOT byte-identical (contentHash all distinct across all 37 rows, 0 exact duplicates found) and do not self-announce as synthetic, so they fail the SYNTHETIC-FIXTURE bar — but they materially undercut the §8.1(a) claim that a dedup migration eliminated story-bank duplication: it appears to prevent byte-exact repeats only, not paraphrase repeats generated by repeated tailoring runs against the same underlying test resume.
ambiguous_escalations.proposed_disposition: ESCALATE — do not auto-delete; needs a human/product decision on whether near-duplicate story consolidation is in scope, since these are algorithm-generated paraphrases tied to genuine underlying career-history content on the test account, not self-announcing fake content.

refs_proof: User-reachability was established by cross-referencing uat/reports/evidence/gold-master-v3/SCREEN-MATRIX.md's route table (lines 46-68), which maps each shipped Next.js page.tsx to the backend GET endpoint it polls and renders. ApprovalRequest -> /dashboard/approvals -> GET /approvals (line 50); Resume -> /dashboard/resume -> GET /resumes (line 52); EmailThread -> /dashboard/email -> GET /emails (line 54); User -> /admin/users -> GET /admin/users (line 63). All confirmed rows sit in tables whose primary access path is scoped by userId matching the logged-in session, so any row is reachable by whoever is authenticated as that owning user (or, for User rows themselves, by an admin session).
approver: risk-officer (GOLD-MASTER-V4 §20.2 designated approver for runtime-path deletions)
corrections_to_proposal: FACTUAL DEFECT IN THE PROPOSAL: the claim that each of the 14 User rows has '0 content rows anywhere' is FALSE. The proposer checked only 8 tables (Job/Application/Resume/AgentRun/StoryEntry/ApprovalRequest/EmailThread/BackgroundJob). The schema has 26 user-referencing columns across 24 tables. Every one of the 14 users owns 1 Subscription + 1 UsageQuota row, and c56667cb7661a0cfef18ada20 additionally owns 3 CareerProfile rows.

STRUCTURAL RISK THE PROPOSAL MISSED: only 8 tables have an ON DELETE CASCADE FK to "User" (AgentRun, Application, ApprovalRequest, Contact, EmailThread, Job, Resume, StoryEntry). 18 further tables carry a userId/actorUserId column with NO FK constraint at all (Subscription, UsageQuota, CareerProfile, AgentConfig, AgentProvider, AgentQuotaBlock, AdminAuditLog, AnthropicOAuthState/Token, BackgroundJob, GmailAccount, GoogleCredential, InterviewSchedule, JobSourceStatus, Offer, OutreachTask, UserProviderCredential, ApprovalRequest.resolvedByUserId). Deleting a User therefore ORPHANS rather than cascades. This is the same defect the prior GOLD-MASTER-V2 review recorded; it is still unfixed.

Executing the manifest exactly as proposed would have left 31 orphan rows (14 Subscription + 14 UsageQuota + 3 CareerProfile) keyed to primary keys that no longer exist, two of them bound to live Stripe customer objects.

DATA IS LIVE AND DRIFTING: StoryEntry was 37 rows at proposal time and is 36 now; AgentRun moved 3663 -> 3664 during this ruling. The manifest is a snapshot, not a lock. Janitor must re-verify each primary key exists immediately before deleting it and must abort on any count mismatch.

rollback_plan.backup_exists_today: NO. There is no database backup on disk and no PITR has been requested for this instance.
rollback_plan.pg_dump_unusable: TESTED THIS RUN AND CONFIRMED BROKEN: the server is PostgreSQL 17.9 but the only client on this VM is PostgreSQL 16.14 (/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin/pg_dump). pg_dump aborts with "aborting because of server version mismatch". pg_dump is therefore NOT an available rollback mechanism and must not be relied on.
rollback_plan.tested_mechanism: psql row-level JSON capture, which works against the 17.9 server from the 16.x client. Executed read-only this run against the real production rows: 47 rows captured (Resume 1, EmailThread 1, User 14, Subscription 14, UsageQuota 14, CareerProfile 3), 20383 bytes, all lines re-parsed successfully with json.loads and 0 unparseable lines.
rollback_plan.MANDATORY_PRECONDITION: Janitor MUST capture every targeted row (and its non-cascading Subscription/UsageQuota/CareerProfile collateral) with row_to_json into cleanup/ROLLBACK-CAPTURE-1.jsonl, verify the file parses and the row count matches the approved manifest, and upload it to s3://abacusai-apps-e154d00a983f92d71946ca64-us-west-2/49362/aether-gmv4-rollback/ BEFORE issuing a single DELETE. No capture, no delete.
rollback_plan.restore_procedure: Each captured line is {"tbl": <table>, "row": {<full column map>}}. Restore with INSERT INTO aether."<tbl>" SELECT * FROM json_populate_record(NULL::aether."<tbl>", :row). Restore parents before children: User -> Subscription/UsageQuota/CareerProfile -> Resume -> EmailThread. Original primary keys are preserved in the capture, so restored rows keep their ids and any surviving reference remains valid.
rollback_plan.execution_discipline: All deletes for one User (User + Subscription + UsageQuota [+ CareerProfile]) run inside a single BEGIN/COMMIT. Verify affected-row counts inside the transaction and ROLLBACK on any deviation from the approved counts.
rollback_plan.residual_risk: The capture restores ROW DATA only. It does not restore anything outside this database - notably the Stripe customer objects - which is a further reason the two Stripe-linked accounts are excluded from this approval.

Every one of the 15 User rows is either the operator or an @example.com address; a query for any User on a non-reserved, non-operator domain returned 0 rows.
blast_radius.if_i_am_wrong: Worst realistic case is the loss of one operator-owned synthetic resume, one operator-owned synthetic email thread, and up to 12 dormant @example.com test logins plus their free-tier entitlement rows. No paying customer, no revenue-bearing subscription and no third-party-owned content is in scope. The excluded items are precisely the ones where being wrong would be expensive.
blast_radius.who_notices: Only the operator (sarkar.vikram@gmail.com). The Resume disappears from /dashboard/resume, the thread from /dashboard/email, and 12 rows from /admin/users. No end user exists to notice.
blast_radius.production_behaviour_change_on_landing: The synthetic "Jane Doe Test Resume" stops rendering on /dashboard/resume and the "NUL byte test subject" thread stops rendering on /dashboard/email - which is the point: both are user-reachable synthetic-fixture surfaces feeding BLOCKER GMV4-approvals-001. /admin/users drops from 15 to 3 rows once the W-K batch runs. No schema change, no code change, no behaviour change for any code path; these are pure data rows. The BLOCKER is NOT fully retired by this manifest because ApprovalRequest ccbe2e7518343e818809f8009 is deliberately retained.
blast_radius.auto_reject_check: Checked: nothing in the approved set appears on the §1.4 PROTECTED or §6.2 DO-NOT-TOUCH lists (packages/db/src/schema.prisma, e2e/auth.setup.ts, Vik_Resume fixture+generator). No force-push, no history rewrite, no schema migration, no bulk purge.

sequencing_ruling.execute_now: The Resume and the EmailThread ONLY. Justification: §23.3 lets a BLOCKER interrupt §20 last-runs-cleanup ordering, these two rows are the user-reachable synthetic-fixture surfaces that constitute BLOCKER GMV4-approvals-001, they are data-only with zero code or FK dependency, and blast radius is near-zero because no real customer data exists. Still gated on the rollback capture precondition.
sequencing_ruling.defer_to_W_K: All 12 approved User rows, together with their 24 non-cascading Subscription/UsageQuota rows. Justification: these are reachable only via the admin-only /admin/users screen, so they contribute nothing to the BLOCKER and earn no §23.3 interrupt. Batching them into W-K keeps the account deletions and the orphan cleanup in one reviewed transaction.
sequencing_ruling.never_without_further_approval: The 2 excluded accounts and the retained ApprovalRequest evidence row.

story_dedup_ruling.ruling: AGREED - the 5 near-duplicate StoryEntry clusters MUST NOT be bulk-deleted. The proposer was right to classify them AMBIGUOUS/ESCALATE, and I am not approving any deletion against StoryEntry.
story_dedup_ruling.root_cause_identified: The migration is not broken - it has never been invoked. apps/api/app/services/story_dedup_migration.py::merge_duplicate_stories has ZERO call sites in production code: grep across apps/ and packages/ finds it only in its own docstring, in a docstring cross-reference in app/services/story_paraphrase.py, and in apps/api/tests/test_we_story_dedup_relevance.py. There is no route, no cron, no admin action and no startup hook that calls it. Its own docstring describes it as operator-triggered. So the §8.1(a) claim that a dedup migration eliminated story-bank duplication is unsupported for existing data: only the create-time forward guard in StoryRepository.create has ever run.
story_dedup_ruling.important_nuance: merge_duplicate_stories MERGES rather than deletes - the oldest row of a group survives with its id, later wording is folded in, and tags/metrics are unioned. That is the correct shape for user-authored career history and must be preserved. Any proposal that converts this into a bulk DELETE is auto-rejected.
preconditions_before_any_story_dedup_tou: Full row_to_json capture of all StoryEntry rows for the target user, verified parseable and uploaded off-box, exactly as for any other production deletion.
A DRY-RUN mode that reports every proposed merge pair with a similarity score and the surviving id, persisted as evidence, with NO writes.

Human review of that dry-run output. BULK_MIGRATION_THRESHOLDS is documented as deliberately more permissive than the create-time preset, so it is tuned to over-match; on user-authored career history a false merge silently rewrites someone history and is not recoverable by regeneration.
Run against the operator/cron account ONLY. It must never run against a real user account until it has been validated on the test account and reviewed.
A verified count reconciliation before and after (the docstring guarantees the row count drops by exactly the reported merged count); abort on any deviation.
Note that StoryEntry drifted from 37 to 36 rows during this ruling, so any dedup run must re-snapshot immediately beforehand rather than trusting the inventory numbers.
story_dedup_ruling.not_a_deletion_approval: This ruling authorises NO write of any kind against StoryEntry. It states the conditions under which a future proposal could be brought to me.
